question.text: Let $\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{rms}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}_2}$ is the r.m.s speed of $\mathrm{H}_2$ at $150 \mathrm{~K}$. At what temperature, the most probable speed of helium $\left[\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{mp}}\right)_{\mathrm{He}}\right]$ will be half of $\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{rms}}\right)_{\mathrm{H}_2}$ ?

solution.text:
$C_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}} \quad C_{m p}=\sqrt{\frac{2 R T}{M}}$
As per question $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{3 \times R \times 150}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 R T}{4}}$ $\mathrm{T}=112.5 \mathrm{~K}$
